account:
Today I have kept my morning office hours and visited the east-bank mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection. No one answered my questions about supplies or deliveries, so I cannot draw conclusions about the grain stores. I have now returned home ahead of noon lunch; council letters, tea, office hours and the eighteen o'clock great-hall presentation remain on my schedule.

The unusual pattern is the activity involving the baker and innkeeper. The secretary's notes record reports of the baker carrying bread at the inn yesterday, and the secretary herself saw the innkeeper with a sack of bread near the plaza. Today Townsfolk Eleven reported the innkeeper carrying a sack at the bakery and mentioned the baker, innkeeper and neighbour being there. Townsfolk Two has repeatedly said 'bridge or port change at bakery,' but I do not know what that phrase means or whether it describes anything they personally witnessed.

My best explanation is preparation for the local baking and hospitality presentation that the innkeeper invited me to attend this evening. The innkeeper explicitly said participating tradespeople would give a short presentation and that I need not prepare. Bread moving between the bakery and inn would fit that explanation, though I have not seen the preparations myself. Perhaps there is an additional arrangement I have not been told about, but I have no evidence of wrongdoing or of a bridge or ferry change. Separately, the treasury ledger remains missing and income, spending and obligations are unknown; nothing I have learned connects that accounting gap to the bread or presentation.
